question.text: In an examination, $62 \%$ of the candidates failed in English, 42% in Mathematics and 20% in both. The number of those who passed in both the subjects is

solution.text: From the given condition, $\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{c}=62 \mathrm{k} ; \mathrm{b}+\mathrm{c}=42 \mathrm{k}$ and $\mathrm{c}=20 \mathrm{k}$ Hence $\mathrm{a}=42 \mathrm{k}$ and $\mathrm{b}=22 \mathrm{k}$ Number of students who failed in none means passed in both $=\mathrm{n}=100 \mathrm{k}-(\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}+\mathrm{c})$ $=100 \mathrm{k}-(42 \mathrm{k}+22 \mathrm{k}+20 \mathrm{k})=16 \mathrm{k}$. or $16 \%$
